The footgun is already documented in consumer code: ConnectScreen.tsx:60-62 has a warning comment ('不能依赖 composio 整对象——useComposio 每 render 返回新字面量，会 effect→setState→re-render 无限循环') and works around it by destructuring. All 16 methods are already useCallback-stable; only the 4 state fields legitimately change.

Consumers: apps/mobile/src/components/app/AppShell.tsx:53,:187,:238,:269; apps/mobile/src/screens/ConnectScreen.tsx:60-62 (documented workaround).

findings.acceptance: In ConnectScreen add temporary console.count('ConnectScreen render'); with the screen visited and React.memo applied (companion finding), open/close the drawer repeatedly — ConnectScreen count must stay flat. findings.title: Unstable callback deps in @pin-ai/state: refresh/[query], patch/[patchMut], refetch/[query] mint new identities every render
findings.problem: Three hooks depend on whole TanStack Query result objects, which are new objects every render: agent-runs.ts refresh useCallback([query]) → new refresh each render → usePipeline's generate useCallback([refreshAgentRuns]) recomputes every render → AppShell's shortcut-ref effect ([toggle, pipeline.generate], AppShell.tsx:76-85) re-runs on every shell render (currently harmless ref writes, but any future consumer putting generate in a dep chain or memo prop inherits the churn). user-settings.ts patch useCallback([patchMut]) and refetch useCallback([query]) are likewise unstable → useAmbientToggle's toggle (deps include patch, useAmbientToggle.ts:96) is never stable → AmbientStatusCard / AmbientScreen memoization of toggle-consuming rows is impossible.
findings.evidence: packages/state/src/queries/agent-runs.ts:49-51 (refresh deps [query]); packages/state/src/queries/user-settings.ts:187-198 (patch deps [patchMut]), :200-202 (refetch deps [query]); downstream: packages/state/src/queries/pipeline.ts:88-132 (generate deps [refreshAgentRuns]); apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientToggle.ts:56-96 (toggle deps include patch). TanStack Query v5 guarantees query.refetch and mutation.mutateAsync are stable function references across renders.
findings.fix: agent-runs.ts: `const { refetch } = query; const refresh = useCallback(async () => { await refetch(); }, [refetch]);`. user-settings.ts: destructure `const { mutateAsync } = patchMut;` and use `[mutateAsync]` as patch's deps (keep the setPatchError logic); refetch: `const { refetch: queryRefetch } = query; useCallback(async () => { await queryRefetch(); }, [queryRefetch])`. No API shape changes.
findings.acceptance: npm run check:packages passes (user-settings.test.tsx and agent-runs consumers exercise these paths). In a dev render-log, pipeline.generate and settings patch identities stay === across consecutive renders (assert via a temporary useEffect(() => console.log('generate changed'), [generate]) in DebugPanel — must log exactly once per mount). Web consumers (proactive-ai-frontend, apps/web) type-check + test green since @pin-ai/state is shared.
findings.risk: Shared package — behavior is identical (mutateAsync/refetch are stable aliases of the same functions); only identity stabilizes. Zero parity risk for proactive-ai-frontend, which benefits equally.

findings.title: AgentRunIndicator: correctly self-subscribed leaf, but the 1s elapsed ticker re-renders the whole chip+dropdown and runs even when nothing displays elapsed
findings.problem: AgentRunIndicator already subscribes to useActiveAgentRuns itself (good — no hoist needed), but setNow(Date.now()) fires every 1000ms whenever runs.length > 0 (AgentRunIndicator.tsx:94-98), re-rendering the entire component — GlassCard chip, dropdown with N RunRows — once per second for the full lifetime of any visible run, including the 30s post-completion grace window where runs.length===1 with a terminal status and summaryDetail is null (:113-116), i.e. the tick repaints with zero visible change. On the 4s poll cadence this component also re-renders from data identity churn (updatedAt/progress on running rows), which is acceptable for a leaf but compounds with the 1s tick.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/app/AgentRunIndicator.tsx:89 (self-subscription), :94-98 (interval keyed only on runs.length), :100 (early return when empty), :113-116 (summaryDetail null for terminal single-run — tick wasted), :148-159 (dropdown rows receive `now` so every tick re-renders all rows).

Additionally wrap the default export in memo() so AppShell renders skip it (it takes no props). Optionally memo(RunRow) keyed on (run, now) — skip; rows are tiny.
findings.acceptance: Trigger a generate: chip shows and elapsed counts up 1s-granular as before. When the run completes (green check, 30s window, dropdown closed): temporary console.count('ARI render') stays flat during the window instead of +1/s. Multi-run dropdown open: elapsed per row still ticks.
findings.risk: If showsElapsed derivation misses a case, elapsed freezes — the acceptance steps above cover both display paths (single-run chip detail, open dropdown).

Grep confirms no client consumer reads ActiveAgentRun.updatedAt/attempts, and .progress is only read on the init-task type (DebugPanel.tsx:241 reads task.progress from useInitTask — a different endpoint), not on ActiveAgentRun.

Consumers of runs fields: AgentRunIndicator.tsx (id/kind/status/startedAt/createdAt/lastError), packages/core/src/machines/pipeline.ts:331-341 (kind/status/id), packages/state/src/queries/pipeline.ts:142-179 (id/kind/status/lastError). No hit for ActiveAgentRun.updatedAt/.attempts/.progress in packages/state, packages/ui-web, apps/mobile (grep over run/agent-filtered matches).

findings.title: Confirmed (deliverable d): drawer drag is UI-thread isolated; the two full-tree re-renders per open/close cycle come from the commit setState, fixed by the memo plan
findings.problem: Verification result, recorded so the implementer doesn't touch the gesture code: MenuDrawerHost's pan gestures write progress.value in onUpdate worklets (no per-frame JS render); the spring runs on the UI thread. JS renders occur at exactly three points: (1) gesture start runOnJS(mountOverlay) → setMounted(true) — MenuDrawerHost re-renders but the children element reference is unchanged, so React bails out of the page subtree; (2) release → runOnJS(commitFromGesture) → onRequestOpen/onRequestClose → AppShell setMenuOpen → full shell re-render → (pre-memo) every mounted keep-alive screen re-reconciles; (3) close-spring completion runOnJS(unmountOverlay) — again subtree bail-out. findings.title: Inline onDecide prop defeats the Entry memo — every chat row re-renders on every Conversation render
findings.problem: ChatScreen deliberately memoizes Entry and builds ref-latest stable callbacks for onRetry/onUpdateQueued/onDeleteQueued/onSendNow/onReply, but renderItem passes `onDecide={(decision, message) => void submitDecision(decision, message)}` as a fresh arrow on every render. memo's shallow compare fails on that one prop, so ALL visible rows re-render on every Conversation render: every streaming transcript tick, every composer keystroke (draft state lives in ChatScreen), every busy flip, every poll-driven parent render. Each defeated row re-runs segmentAssistantParts, rebuilds WorkGroup/MarkdownText element trees, and recomputes plainText (flatMap+join). This is the concrete mechanism behind baseline P7's 'transcript fan-out' — fixing it makes the existing memo actually work.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx:576 (`onDecide={(decision, message) => void submitDecision(decision, message)}` inline in renderItem), :68 (Entry = memo(...)), :464-488 (ref-latest pattern already used for the other five callbacks — onDecide is the only one missed), :108-111 (plainText flatMap+join runs every Entry render even while entry.running, though only consumed at :164 when !running).
findings.fix: In Conversation (ChatScreen.tsx), mirror the existing ref-latest pattern: `const decideRef = useRef(submitDecision); decideRef.current = submitDecision; const onDecide = useCallback((d: "approve" | "reject", m?: string) => void decideRef.current(d, m), []);` and pass `onDecide={onDecide}` in renderItem (line 576). Also hoist renderItem itself into a useCallback keyed on [channel, handleRetry, onUpdateQueued, onDeleteQueued, onSendNow, onReply, busy, hitlHostId, awaitingDecision, onDecide] and hoist keyExtractor to module scope. Inside Entry, move the plainText computation behind the `!entry.running` branch (or wrap in useMemo on [entry.parts, entry.running]) so streaming ticks skip it.
findings.acceptance: Add a temporary render counter (console.count or why-did-you-render) inside Entry. Before: typing one character in the composer increments the counter for every visible row. After: typing increments zero row counters; during streaming only the entry whose parts changed increments. Remove counter after verification.
findings.risk: Low. submitDecision via ref-latest matches the file's established pattern; only stale-closure risk is if submitDecision identity carries state, which it does not (runtime function). Verify HITL approve/reject still works end-to-end in a card chat.

findings.title: CardActionsProvider context value is a new object every AppShell render, and useCardActions callbacks churn via the unstable composio literal
findings.problem: The provider builds `const value = { ...actions, composio }` inline each render (comment claims 'no memo value', which is wrong once consumers get memoized). AppShell re-renders every 4-30s from usePipeline/useComposio polls (baseline P5); each render produces a new context value identity, so every consumer re-renders: NowScreen, every TasksScreen Row (each Row calls useCardActionsContext), and mounted CardDetailSheets — even when none of the five Sets changed. Worse, memoizing the value naively won't help: useCardActions' `confirm` depends on `composio`, and useComposio returns a new object literal every render (documented at ConnectScreen.tsx:60-61), so `confirm`'s identity changes every AppShell render, poisoning any useMemo. This is the prerequisite for baseline P5/P6 memoization to have any effect on card rows.

findings.title: AmbientScreen re-renders every ≤5s forever (even hidden) and rebuilds its whole timeline derivation in the render body
findings.problem: Three independent re-render pumps hit AmbientScreen, which is keep-alive mounted permanently after first visit: (a) useAmbientTimeline polls SQLite every 5s and unconditionally setStates three NEW arrays each cycle (no change detection) — guaranteed screen re-render every 5s, hidden or not, plus the SQLite queries themselves; (b) useAmbientLiveSession runs a second 5s interval plus per-transcript-event updates; (c) the ambient status subscription stores a full fresh RuntimeStatus snapshot object on EVERY notifyStatus (which fires on every captured signal — motion/location/sound/transcript), though the screen consumes only `firstSourceError`. Every one of those re-renders rebuilds `timelineEntries` (three maps + full sort), `priorityEntries`/`otherEntries` filters, and `visibleTimelineEntries` in the render body with no useMemo, then re-reconciles the entire non-virtualized timeline (baseline P4's rows). With ambient ON this is a constant background CPU tax on the JS thread even while the user is on NOW or in a chat.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientTimeline.ts:94 (`setInterval(() => void load(), 5_000)`, no page-active gate), :56-75 (load() always sets new arrays: setEvents/setPendingTranscriptWindows/setLatestRawEvents with fresh .filter results); apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientLiveSession.ts:134 (second `setInterval(..., 5000)`); apps/mobile/src/screens/AmbientScreen.tsx:152-156 (subscribeAmbientStatus → setRuntimeStatus(ambientStatusSnapshot())), :157-158 (only firstSourceError consumed); apps/mobile/src/ambient/runtime.ts:389-414 (ambientStatusSnapshot builds a fresh object + sources.map every call); apps/mobile/src/ambient/status.ts:85-87,107 (notifyStatus fires per recordSourceEvent); AmbientScreen.tsx:188-199 (timelineEntries map+sort+filters in render body, no useMemo).
findings.fix: Four surgical changes: (1) AmbientScreen.tsx:152-156 — replace the whole-snapshot subscription with an error-only selector: `const update = () => { const err = ambientStatusSnapshot().sources.find(s => s.lastError)?.lastError ?? null; setFirstSourceError(prev => prev === err ? prev : err); }` (state becomes a string|null). (2) Gate both 5s intervals on page visibility: pass a `paused`/`active` boolean into useAmbientTimeline and useAmbientLiveSession (AmbientScreen already imports usePageActive) and skip creating the interval when inactive, with an immediate load() on reactivation. (3) In useAmbientTimeline.load(), skip setState when content is unchanged — cheapest robust check: compare a fingerprint `rows.map(r=>r.id+r.updatedAt).join()` (and equivalents for pending/latestRaw) against a ref before setting. (4) AmbientScreen.tsx:188-199 — wrap timelineEntries in `useMemo(..., [events, pendingTranscriptWindows, latestRawEvents, dismiss])` and derive priority/other/visible inside the same memo keyed additionally on visibleCount.
findings.acceptance: With ambient ON, navigate to NOW and idle 60s: profiler shows zero AmbientScreen commits (currently ~12+). Return to Ambient: timeline refreshes within one poll cycle and live-session card still streams transcripts. Source-error subtitle still appears when a source errors.

Fingerprint comparison must include dismissed/visibility changes or dismiss() will look like a no-op; dismiss() already calls load() explicitly which recomputes the fingerprint, so covered — verify dismiss still removes the row.

findings.title: MarkdownText re-runs splitBlocks per streaming tick and uses index keys for blocks (correct but fragile) — document as guarded, add cheap memo
findings.problem: MarkdownText calls `splitBlocks(text)` in its body on every render — for the streaming entry this is O(text length) per token tick, on top of the Block-level memo that correctly prevents re-PARSING completed blocks (the expensive part). The index key (`key={i}`) is safe only because blocks are append-only/last-block-mutating; if a future change re-splits earlier blocks the memo silently thrashes. Keep index keys but add a one-line comment stating the append-only invariant so a future editor doesn't 'fix' them to content-hash keys (which would defeat memo for the mutating tail block).

findings.risk: None — pure memoization; the comment prevents regression.

findings.title: Chat list (P7 root cause): inline onDecide lambda at ChatScreen.tsx:576 busts memo(Entry) for every visible row on every streaming tick — fix identity, then tune FlatList windowing in place

findings.title: Chat-open waterfall: SQLite local-history read is awaited before the authoritative network history fetch starts
findings.problem: In the conversation connect loop, the local-first read (`await localHistoryRef.current(...)`) fully resolves before conversationHistory() is even issued. The local read includes lazy DB open + ensureSyncSchema on first touch (apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/expo-database.ts:11-19, packages/core/src/sync/schema.ts:80-95) and shares the engine's serial queue with any in-flight boot full-pass — so on cold start, opening chat can queue the SQLite read behind a multi-page message sync, delaying the network fetch that actually paints the fresh transcript. The two sources are independent; nothing requires them to be sequential.
findings.evidence: packages/state/src/queries/conversation.ts:262-337 — isResume block: :269 `await localHistoryRef.current?.(session, HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE)` then :282 `await conversationHistory(session, ...)`; the merge at :304 ('resync') is a full rebuild so late-arriving local data must not overwrite network data. Serial-queue contention: apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/sync-bootstrap.ts:63-68 readLocalHistory -> scheduler.readLocalHistory; note scheduler.readLocalHistory (packages/core/src/sync/scheduler.ts:163-171) actually bypasses serialize() — reads are direct db.query — so the contention is only SQLite-level, but the sequential await stands regardless.
findings.fix: In conversation.ts connect(): start both concurrently — `const localP = localHistoryRef.current?.(session, HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE) ?? Promise.resolve(null); const networkP = conversationHistory(session, {signal, limit: HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE});` then `const localPage = await Promise.race-free pattern`: await localP with .catch(()=>null); apply the local dispatch ONLY if the network promise hasn't already resolved — simplest correct sequencing: `let networkDone = false; void networkP.finally(()=>{networkDone=true});` apply local resync when `localPage && !cancelled && !networkDone`; then `const page = await networkP` and run the existing authoritative resync unconditionally. This keeps 'local paints first when it wins, network always corrects' semantics with zero added latency to the network path.
findings.acceptance: Instrument temporarily: log timestamps for local-applied and network-request-sent; verify network request now fires within ~1ms of connect() vs after local read (previously ms-to-hundreds-of-ms on cold DB). Chat first-paint from local still works offline (airplane mode: transcript renders from SQLite). Existing conversation replay tests in core remain green (npm run check:packages).
findings.risk: Ordering bug potential: if local resolves after network, applying it would clobber fresher data — the networkDone flag guards this; add a unit test for 'slow local, fast network' ordering. Shared with web ChatScreen path (proactive-ai-frontend native) — same win there.

findings.title: Duplicate usePipeline instances (AppShell + DebugPanel): two divergent RunStates, double /status fetch, and no RN persistence parity
findings.problem: usePipeline is instantiated twice on RN — AppShell (for Siri shortcut generate + cards invalidation on complete) and DebugPanel (Generate button + run banner). Each instance holds independent RunState, fires its own mount /status GET, and reconciles independently via the agent-runs feed: a generate started from DebugPanel leaves AppShell's instance idle until orphan adoption catches it on a poll tick (up to 4s later), and AppShell's 'run complete -> invalidate cards' effect (AppShell.tsx:90-95) is driven by its own instance so it works only because orphan adoption eventually converges. DebugPanel's hooks run even while the panel is closed (it returns null only at :413, after all hooks). Additionally usePipeline's persist option (web passes sessionStorage) is not wired on RN, so RunState dies with the JS process — acceptable (orphan adoption recovers) but should be an explicit decision, not an accident.

Tap Generate in DebugPanel: AppShell's lastCompleteRunIdRef effect fires on completion (cards invalidate immediately — observe [sync]/TQ devtools or a temp log) without waiting for an agent-runs poll tick to adopt an orphan. findings.title: Cards freshness relies on a permanent 30s full-payload poll; foreground push notifications are not used to invalidate, and the poll never pauses
findings.problem: useCardsQuery refetches GET /cards?limit=200 (full card payloads for 200 cards) every 30s for the entire app session — NowScreen and TasksScreen share the key so it's one request, but it runs even when the user sits in Chat/Settings/Profile for minutes (keep-alive pages keep observers mounted, so the interval never stops while the app is foregrounded). Meanwhile the backend already pushes 'new card' APNs notifications, and apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts registers the token but installs NO addNotificationReceivedListener — a foreground push about a new card does nothing to the cache; the user still waits up to 30s. Event-driven invalidation already covers the other freshness sources (card-chat turn done: ChatScreen.tsx:373-376; generate complete: AppShell.tsx:90-95), so the poll is pure backstop and can be relaxed once push-invalidate lands.

(1) Push-invalidation: in apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts (or a small push-listeners.ts wired from App.tsx after login) add `Notifications.addNotificationReceivedListener(() => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: cardsKeys.all }))` and `addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` doing the same (tap-from-background); import queryClient from lib/query-client. (2) Relax the poll: add an opt to useCardsQuery — `poll?: boolean` (default true) mapped to `refetchInterval: poll ? POLL_INTERVAL_MS : false`; NowScreen passes its `active` prop || view-is-now, TasksScreen passes usePageActive(); because keep-alive pages never remount, pair with an on-activate refresh: in each screen, effect on pageActive false->true -> `queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: cardsKeys.all})` guarded by dataUpdatedAt older than 30s (read via queryClient.getQueryState). Web apps unaffected (poll opt defaults true; web callers unchanged).

findings.title: usePipeline subscribes to the full agent-runs array — every 4s poll payload change re-renders AppShell (data-layer half of P5)
findings.problem: useActiveAgentRuns returns the raw runs array; while any run is in flight the 4s poll returns rows whose volatile fields (progress counters, updatedAt) change every tick, defeating TQ structural sharing, so AppShell (which holds usePipeline -> useActiveAgentRuns) re-renders on every tick and re-reconciles all keep-alive screens (baseline P5). But usePipeline only consumes a narrow projection: the generator-kind runs' {id, kind, status, lastError} (pipeline.ts effects match on kind/id/status). A select-based subscription makes AppShell's data identity stable across ticks where nothing it cares about changed — complementing (not replacing) the React.memo work owned by the render dimension.
findings.evidence: packages/state/src/queries/agent-runs.ts:41-47 useQuery returns full data, no select; packages/state/src/queries/pipeline.ts:80 `const { runs, refresh } = useActiveAgentRuns()`, :140-180 effect reads only kind/id/status/lastError, :188-196 reads only id, :203-209 findOrphanGeneratorRun (kind+status). In pipeline.ts replace useActiveAgentRuns() with a projection selecting `runs.filter(r => r.kind.startsWith('generator')).map(({id, kind, status, lastError}) => ({id, kind, status, lastError}))` — TQ memoizes select results by structural sharing, so ticks that only mutate progress/updatedAt of a dream run (or heartbeat fields of the generator) produce a referentially-identical projection and zero re-render of AppShell/DebugPanel. Keep `refresh` via a queryClient.invalidateQueries wrapper (refetch() needs the observer; invalidate on the key is equivalent here). The refetchInterval callback still needs full data — it reads q.state.data which remains the unselected cache value in v5 (verify: in v5 refetchInterval receives the Query, state.data is post-select for the observer? No — refetchInterval is per-observer and q.state.data is the QUERY cache data, unselected; confirm with a unit test).
findings.acceptance: Add a React Profiler check or temp render counter in AppShell: with a dream run in flight (4s ticks), AppShell renders drop from ~1/tick to only on status transitions. usePipeline behavior unchanged: generate -> running -> complete flow, orphan adoption, F5-equivalent recovery all pass existing pipeline tests (npm run check:packages).

findings.title: SQLite local-first extension design: reuse the existing engine for cards read-path + memories/profile mirrors — incremental, no rewrite
findings.problem: The sync engine today covers: threads + messages delta sync (cursor-based /sync/threads + /sync/messages, engine.ts:84-180), cards full-mirror (200-row upsert from /cards, engine.ts:186-232, explicitly 'FTS index source, read path stays TQ+persister' per :185 comment), generic outbox, and FTS5 search (messages_fts/cards_fts) — with read paths wired only for chat history (ChatScreen.tsx:403 main thread, CardDetailSheet.tsx:626 card runs). Missing for a full local-first story: profile/memories have no local mirror (cold-start covered by finding #1's persister expansion, but offline capacity beyond 24h maxAge, per-user isolation, and future search need SQLite), and searchLocal() covers only messages+cards. Also note a latent duplication: syncCards hits GET /cards on every full pass (30min fallback + boot) while TQ separately polls the same endpoint — harmless today, but the extension should unify rather than add a third fetcher.
findings.evidence: Schema: packages/core/src/sync/schema.ts:10-70 (v1 threads/messages, v2 cards/outbox/FTS). Scheduler pass: packages/core/src/sync/scheduler.ts:92-120 (drain -> threads -> main-thread messages -> cards; :67-72 only kind='main' threads full-passed, card threads sync via doorbell only). Read paths: apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/sync-bootstrap.ts:63-76; per-user DB naming :32 `pinai_sync_${userId}`. onNewCards platform hook exists: scheduler.ts:33-36,105-107 (unused on RN — iOS uses APNs).

PHASE A (do now, near-free): after finding #1, persister covers cold-start for profile/memories/devices — no SQLite work; explicitly record in schema.ts header that persister is the read cache and SQLite is the search/offline tier. PHASE B (cards local read, small): add core/sync/local-read.ts `readLocalCards(db): Promise<VisibleCardEntry[]|null>` deserializing payload_json/score_json/latest_outcome (columns already stored, engine.ts:202-218); in sync-bootstrap.ts export it; in RN NowScreen pass it as useCardsQuery initialData-style seed: on startSync completion (add SyncSchedulerOpts.onCardsSynced?(entries) callback next to onNewCards, invoked in runFullPass after syncCards with the upserted entries) call queryClient.setQueryData(cardsKeys.list(200), entries) ONLY when getQueryState(...).dataUpdatedAt is older than the sync — this replaces neither the poll nor the persister, it makes the 30min engine fetch feed the UI instead of being write-only, and gives >24h offline cards. PHASE C (memories/profile mirrors, only when offline-profile or global search is prioritized): schema v3 migration appended to MIGRATIONS — `CREATE TABLE memories (memory_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, synced_at INTEGER NOT NULL); CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE memories_fts USING fts5(text, memory_id UNINDEXED); CREATE TABLE kv_snapshots (domain TEXT PRIMARY KEY, payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, synced_at INTEGER NOT NULL);` — memories sync mirrors the syncCards pattern (server has no delta endpoint for memories; full upsert of active memories via fetchMemories({status:'active', limit:200}) is the same server-authoritative small-table strategy engine.ts:185 already justifies; do NOT build a /sync/memories delta endpoint until row counts justify it), profile snapshot goes into kv_snapshots('profile'). Extend runFullPass with engine.syncMemories()+syncProfile() behind the same serialize(); extend searchLocal() with memories_fts. TQ read: same onXSynced -> setQueryData seam as Phase B. Never move conversation streaming state or agent-runs into SQLite.

Engine tests: extend engine.test.ts replay suite (better-sqlite3) with onCardsSynced + readLocalCards round-trip. Phase C: searchLocal('term') returns memory hits; migration v2->v3 applies on existing device DB without data loss (PRAGMA user_version=3).

findings.title: Card-thread local-history policy is inconsistent: ChatScreen disables SQLite reads for card chats while CardDetailSheet enables them for the same threads
findings.problem: Two RN surfaces read the same card-thread history with opposite local-first policies. ChatScreen passes localHistory only for the main thread, with a comment claiming card threads must stay cloud-authoritative to avoid 'painting another card's stale SQLite rows' — but readLocalHistoryPage filters by thread_id, so cross-card contamination is not actually possible; the real staleness risk (within-thread outdated rows) is corrected by the authoritative network resync in the same connect cycle (conversation.ts:282-331), identical to the main-thread path that already trusts it. findings.title: Voice Waveform: 36 concurrent JS-thread core-Animated loops animating layout `height` with useNativeDriver:false
findings.problem: voice/Waveform.tsx builds 18 bars, each driven by an Animated.loop(Animated.sequence([timing, timing])) with `useNativeDriver: false`, and each bar's style animates `height` (a layout prop) plus interpolated opacity. That is 18 loops x 2 timings running entirely on the JS thread: every frame the JS driver computes 18 values, crosses to native, and each height change dirties layout. This runs exactly while voice capture is active — concurrently with the ASR streaming / recording pipeline on the same JS thread — so it competes with transcription updates and drops both animation and app responsiveness frames. It is the only remaining core-Animated (non-Reanimated) animation in the app.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/voice/Waveform.tsx:15 (18 Animated.Value), :23-42 (Animated.loop/sequence with useNativeDriver:false at :30 and :35), :47-59 (height via value.interpolate + opacity interpolate). Consumers: components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:144 (active while captureStatus==="listening") and voice/VoiceButton.tsx:96.
findings.fix: Rewrite Waveform with Reanimated worklets, matching the codebase norm: (1) one `useSharedValue` per bar (or a single clock shared value with per-bar phase math inside useAnimatedStyle); start with `withRepeat(withSequence(withTiming(1,{duration:380+(i%5)*55}), withTiming(0.25,{duration:360+(i%3)*70})), -1)` plus `withDelay((i%4)*45, ...)` to keep the exact stagger. (2) Animate `transform:[{scaleY}]` instead of `height` — give each bar a fixed height of its max (22-(i%3)*3) and scaleY from 5/max..1, so no layout pass ever runs; keep the opacity interpolation in the same useAnimatedStyle. (3) Gate on the existing `active` prop with cancelAnimation in cleanup (current stopAnimation logic maps 1:1). Bars are 2.5px wide with borderRadius 999; scaleY distortion of the round caps at this width is imperceptible.

findings.title: Un-gated infinite Reanimated loops on always-mounted surfaces: NOW BreatheHalo, AskPinAiBar chevron, and chat's ShimmerText/WorkGroup-Spin/PulseDot keep running while hidden

ChatSheet always mounted (AppShell.tsx:263, ChatSheet.tsx header '常 mount'); CardChatScreen always mounted (AppShell.tsx:275). PageActiveContext exists but is module-private (KeepAlivePage.tsx:20) and defaults true outside pages, so chat sheets currently read 'active'.

(3) In each loop component, gate the loop on visibility: `const active = usePageActive();` then `useEffect(() => { if (!active) { cancelAnimation(sv); sv.value = <rest pose>; return; } sv.value = withRepeat(...); return () => cancelAnimation(sv); }, [active])`. Apply to ShimmerText (ui/ShimmerText.tsx:31), WorkGroup Spin (:47), ProposeActionCard PulseDot (:90). findings.title: Full-screen scrim BlurViews animated via ancestor opacity during drawer/sheet gestures — per-frame live blur re-render for a 2-4px design blur
findings.problem: MenuDrawer's scrim is a full-screen expo-blur BlurView(8) inside an Animated.View whose opacity tracks finger progress 1:1; CardDetailSheet's dim layer is a full-screen BlurView(10) with opacity derived from panel y every frame; GoalDetailSheet copies the same pattern (BlurView 10). During every drawer drag / sheet spring frame, iOS's UIVisualEffectView re-samples the entire underlying content (which is itself changing: panel translating, dim fading), i.e. a full-screen offscreen render pass per frame on top of the gesture. Additionally, fractional alpha on a UIVisualEffectView ancestor is Apple-documented undefined rendering (blur + alpha don't compose correctly). The design source is backdrop-blur-sm(4px) / blur(2px) — a barely visible effect paid for at full-screen live-blur price precisely during the most latency-sensitive moments (follow-finger gestures). The team already accepts flatten trades (SphereCards.tsx:11-13 dropped per-frame blur sampling).
findings.evidence: components/app/MenuDrawer.tsx:200-205 (Animated dimStyle opacity wrapping BlurView intensity=8 + tint), :182 (dimStyle = opacity: progress.value, updated every gesture frame at :155/:167); components/now/CardDetailSheet.tsx:673-677 (dimStyle opacity wrapping BlurView intensity=10), :623 (dimStyle recomputed from y each frame); components/profile/GoalDetailSheet.tsx:165 (same dim BlurView 10). Also MenuDrawer panel BlurView(75) at :208 sits under a 0.85→0.95 white gradient (:209-212) — ≥85% opaque cover means the blur contributes almost nothing visually while re-sampling during the whole panel translation.
findings.fix: Flatten the scrims: delete the scrim BlurViews and keep only the tint views — MenuDrawer.tsx:202 (keep styles.scrimTint fg/10), CardDetailSheet.tsx:675 (keep styles.dimTint fg/5), GoalDetailSheet.tsx:165 (keep its tint). Slightly raise tint alpha if the flattened scrim reads too light on device (e.g. fg/10 → fg/12) — judged on device per pixel-parity rule. For the MenuDrawer panel (:208): drop BlurView(75) as well — under 0.85-0.95 white gradient the delta is near-nil; if the owner rejects that on device, keep panel blur (it's only 224px wide) and take the scrim wins only. Do NOT touch CardDetailSheet/GoalDetailSheet panel blurs (intensity 65 under 0.5-0.7 white — genuinely visible glass).
findings.acceptance: Drawer follow-finger drag and card-drawer spring hold 60/120fps on device (Instruments Core Animation: offscreen-rendered passes during drag drop by one full-screen pass per removed BlurView). Side-by-side screenshots of open drawer/sheet vs dev app approved by owner.
findings.risk: Visual parity: background behind scrim is ~2-4px sharper than dev. Owner sign-off on device required (rn-migration-pixel-parity); tint alpha may need +0.02 compensation.

findings.title: KeepAlivePage first-visit fade-in starts in the same commit as the heavy screen mount; drawer close spring, cross-fade, and Fabric mount all stack on one frame
findings.problem: Complement to baseline P2 (do not re-plan P2 itself). KeepAlivePage starts `withTiming(opacity→1, 180ms)` in a useEffect that runs in the very commit where a first-visit screen (10-43KB trees per P2) mounts, and MenuDrawer's onNavigate fires `navigate(id)` + `setMenuOpen(false)` in the same JS tick (AppShell), so the Fabric mount commit (main thread), the drawer close spring, and both cross-fade timings all contend for the same frames — the 180ms fade's first frames are eaten by the mount and the drawer visibly hitches. Even after P2's startTransition lands, the fade will still start before the transition commit has painted unless it is sequenced off first layout.
findings.evidence: components/app/KeepAlivePage.tsx:34-43 (withTiming starts in useEffect on active, same commit as first mount since KeepAlivePage and child mount together via visited-gate at AppShell.tsx:217-256); AppShell.tsx:196-200 (onNavigate: navigate(id) + setMenuOpen(false) synchronously); MenuDrawer.tsx:172-180 (close spring effect fires on the same re-render).
findings.fix: Two sequencing changes: (1) KeepAlivePage — start the fade from the child's first layout instead of the mount commit: keep initial opacity 0, add `onLayout` on the Animated.View that (once, via ref flag) kicks `opacity.value = withTiming(1, {duration: FADE_MS})`; subsequent activations (already-mounted pages) keep the current useEffect path. This guarantees the fade plays its full 180ms after the expensive commit instead of being swallowed by it. (2) AppShell/MenuDrawer — when navigation originates from the drawer, close the drawer first and defer the mount one frame: in AppShell's onNavigate, call setMenuOpen(false) synchronously, then `requestAnimationFrame(() => navigate(id))` (or InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions if the drawer spring should fully finish; rAF is enough since the spring runs on the UI thread and only the Fabric commit stalls it). Coordinate with the P2 implementer: if P2 wraps setVisited in startTransition, item (2) becomes the transition's natural behavior and only item (1) is still needed.
findings.acceptance: First navigation to Profile/Ambient from the drawer: drawer close spring plays without a dropped-frame hitch (slow-motion screen recording), and the incoming page's fade is a full visible 180ms instead of popping in mid-fade.
findings.risk: One-frame delay before the new page starts appearing (imperceptible; the old page remains visible). onLayout-once flag must reset never (keep-alive pages mount once).

findings.title: Drawer overlay (2 BlurViews + gradient + 6 items) mounts on the JS thread mid-gesture at pan activation
findings.problem: MenuDrawer's open pan calls `runOnJS(mountOverlay)` in onStart — which fires only after the 18px activation threshold, i.e. the finger is already moving and the panel must appear under it. The overlay subtree (full-screen scrim BlurView, 224px panel BlurView(75) + LinearGradient, 6 icon+label rows) then mounts on the busy JS thread; until that commit lands, the follow-finger frames show nothing (progress is being written to a not-yet-mounted panel), producing a start-of-gesture hitch on the drawer's edge-pull path.
findings.evidence: components/app/MenuDrawer.tsx:145-153 (openPan .activeOffsetX(-18) → onStart runOnJS(mountOverlay)), :193-253 (mounted ? <FullBleedOverlay>… full overlay tree), :137/:177-179 (unmountOverlay when close spring finishes — so every open remounts from scratch).

A display:none UIVisualEffectView does no per-frame sampling, so idle cost is only retained memory (~one full-screen blur layer + panel). First-ever open still mounts mid-gesture; optionally pre-warm once post-login via the same idle timer AppShell already uses for prefetch (AppShell.tsx:100-128) by mounting the overlay hidden. Note: if the F5 scrim-blur flatten lands first, the mount cost shrinks and this can be re-evaluated — implement F5 first, then measure.
findings.acceptance: Slow-motion recording of an edge-pull: panel is visible under the finger within 1 frame of crossing the 18px threshold on 2nd+ opens (previously several frames blank while mounting).
findings.risk: Retained memory for the hidden overlay (one screen-sized blur layer). Ensure pointerEvents are disabled while hidden (display:none suffices) so the invisible overlay never eats touches.

findings.title: AuroraBackground: @shopify/react-native-skia pod shipped and 2 full-screen Canvas surfaces kept resident for a fully static image
findings.problem: AuroraBackground draws 6 static radial-gradient ovals in a Skia Canvas. Skia is used NOWHERE else in the app, yet: (1) the whole react-native-skia framework (~8-12MB binary, dylib load + GPU context init at first Canvas mount) ships for one static picture; (2) ChatSheet and CardChatScreen are always mounted from login, so two full-screen Skia surfaces (~14MB GPU memory each on a 3x device) sit resident even when both sheets are closed off-screen. The content never invalidates (static props), so there is no per-frame draw cost — the waste is binary size, startup dylib/GPU-context cost, and resident GPU memory x2 (x3 while LoginScreen is up).
findings.evidence: ui/AuroraBackground.tsx:17 (skia import), :69-73 (Canvas with static SPOTS); grep confirms sole consumer of @shopify/react-native-skia (apps/mobile/package.json:28); always-mounted consumers: components/app/ChatSheet.tsx:59 + AppShell.tsx:263, screens/CardChatScreen.tsx:141 + AppShell.tsx:275; LoginScreen.tsx:125.
findings.fix: Replace the Skia Canvas with react-native-svg (already a dependency — AiSphere.tsx:11, LoginScreen GoogleG): an `<Svg>` absolute-fill containing 6 `<Ellipse fill="url(#g{i})">` each with an `<RadialGradient>` in Defs using the identical cx/cy/rx/ry/color/0→0.6-stop math from SPOTS (SkiaSpot maps 1:1 to SVG RadialGradient with gradientUnits=userSpaceOnUse, r=max(rx,ry) — same as vec/r today; the transparent same-hue end color trick carries over verbatim). SVG renders once into the view's normal backing store — no separate GPU surface, no Skia runtime. Then remove @shopify/react-native-skia from package.json and re-run pod install via prebuild. Alternative (even cheaper at runtime, slightly less exact): pre-render the 6 spots into a PNG and stack it over bg-gradient.jpg with resizeMode stretch — spots are percentage-positioned so stretching preserves layout; choose SVG first since it is pixel-exact per-device.
findings.acceptance: Pixel-compare screenshots of chat sheet / card chat / login before vs after (owner verifies on device). App .ipa size drops by the Skia framework size (measure archive before/after). No skia import remains (grep).
findings.risk: SVG radial gradient interpolation can differ subtly from Skia's at the feathered edge — verify no banding/gray fringe on device (the same-hue alpha-0 end color already guards the gray-edge case). AuroraBackground.web.tsx exists for web parity and is untouched.

findings.title: Chat transcript rows carry live BlurViews (WorkGroup, NotifyCard, feedback bar, landing chips) that re-sample on every scroll/streaming frame
findings.problem: Each WorkGroup block, NotifyCard, and CardResultFeedbackBar in the transcript embeds an expo-blur BlurView, and MainChatLanding renders 3 more in its suggestion chips. These are UIVisualEffectViews INSIDE list rows: whenever the FlatList scrolls, every visible one re-samples the content behind it per frame; during streaming (P7: every transcript update re-renders rows) the sampled region invalidates continuously. A long conversation shows several simultaneously. What's behind them is the static AuroraBackground — blurring a static, near-uniform backdrop yields an almost constant color, so the live blur buys nearly nothing visually. findings.evidence: components/chat/WorkGroup.tsx:314 (BlurView 24 per work group), components/chat/NotifyCard.tsx:39 (BlurView 24 per notify row), components/chat/CardResultFeedbackBar.tsx:66 (BlurView 20), components/chat/MainChatLanding.tsx:61 (BlurView 20 x3 chips). Static backdrop: ChatSheet.tsx:59 / CardChatScreen.tsx:141 AuroraBackground (static per its own header). Fixed-chrome blurs to KEEP (genuinely blur moving transcript content): ChatComposer.tsx:125,161; JumpToLatest.tsx:47; CardContextHeaderSlot.tsx:37.

Keep the composer/header/jump-pill blurs untouched. If the owner rejects flat fills for parity, fallback: keep BlurView only in MainChatLanding (static, 3 chips, no scroll) and flatten just the transcript-row ones (WorkGroup/NotifyCard/CardResultFeedbackBar) where scroll cost is real.

findings.risk: Visual parity: glass effect on rows becomes a constant tint — near-identical over the static aurora, but the owner must approve on device (dev Capacitor iOS does render these blurs live).

findings.problem: Reanimated repeat animations keep driving their shared value on the UI thread after the owning component unmounts (until GC), so every unmounted spinner/pulse leaves a zombie frame callback. Individually small, but these mount/unmount constantly (chat tool spins, connect spinners, sheet status spinners) and the leaks accumulate within a session.

Where finding #3 adds active-gating to the same effects, fold both into the one effect there — do not double-touch. Optionally extract the repeated 800ms-Loader2 spin into ui/Spinner (WorkGroup/CardDetailSheet/AgentRunIndicator each hand-roll the identical component) — only if the owner wants the dedupe; the cancelAnimation additions alone satisfy this finding.
findings.acceptance: grep shows every withRepeat in apps/mobile/src has a matching cancelAnimation cleanup (or is gated by the finding-#3 active effect). Open/close a card sheet 10x mid-run: no residual UI-thread frame callbacks (Reanimated debug or perf monitor idle).

findings.title: AgentRunIndicator keeps spinning + re-rendering every second while covered by full-screen chat sheets
findings.problem: The runs chip (Loader2 spin loop + a 1s setInterval setState for the elapsed label, which re-renders the GlassCard/gradient subtree) stays mounted and active while ChatSheet or CardChatScreen fully covers it — exactly the period when a run is most likely in flight, so it spins invisibly for the entire run. findings.title: GlassCard: 4-view/2-shadow recipe multiplied across Ambient timeline rows — flatten one view and the near-invisible outer shadow
findings.problem: Complement to baseline P4 (virtualization is the main fix; this reduces per-row cost that survives it). findings.title: Metro inlineRequires is OFF — the entire app module graph (all 7 screens + 1,713-icon lucide barrel + markdown/webview/skia) executes at module-eval before first paint
findings.problem: Expo SDK 56's default getTransformOptions returns `inlineRequires: false`, and metro.config.js does not override it. With eager requires, importing AppShell from App.tsx transitively EXECUTES every screen module and everything they import at boot, before the BootScreen ever paints. Verified boot order (everything below runs before first paint): index.ts polyfills (url-polyfill, cond. fast-text-encoding, expo-crypto shims) → App.tsx module-eval: global.css (NativeWind), transport-bootstrap (→ env.ts fail-fast, supabase createClient + AppState listener at supabase.ts:12-28), i18n (96 locale JSONs + sync i18n.init — P8), 8 font-weight asset modules, @pin-ai/core+state, sync-bootstrap, ambient/runtime (+ all ambient sources), push.ts (Notifications.setNotificationHandler at :23), AppShell → ALL screens (AppShell.tsx:27-33: CardChat/Connect/Setting/Now/Tasks/Ambient/Profile) → their transitive graph: lucide barrel (64 import sites), react-native-markdown-display (MarkdownText.tsx), react-native-webview (BrowserPanel.tsx), @shopify/react-native-skia (AuroraBackground.tsx), OnboardingFlow, VideoBackdrop, voice/ → then module-scope registrations (App.tsx:52-60) → first render → BootScreen paint. This is pure JS-thread serial cost on every cold start, and it is what makes P2's 'first-visit mount' only half the story — the module EVAL of those screens is also paid, at boot.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/metro.config.js:11 — only `withNativeWind(getDefaultConfig(__dirname))`, no getTransformOptions override. node_modules/@expo/metro-config/build/ExpoMetroConfig.js:323-328 — `getTransformOptions: async () => ({ transform: { experimentalImportSupport: true, inlineRequires: false } })`; runtime-verified by executing the config: both dev:true and dev:false return inlineRequires:false. apps/mobile/src/components/app/AppShell.tsx:27-33 — static imports of all 7 screens. apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:14-46 — the full import list above. Side-effect-order-critical modules are all BARE imports (App.tsx:14,15,18 — global.css / transport-bootstrap / i18n; index.ts:5), which inlineRequires never defers (only requires whose binding is used get inlined) — so boot-order invariants survive the flip.
findings.fix: In apps/mobile/metro.config.js, after the withNativeWind call (line 11) add: `config.transformer.getTransformOptions = async () => ({ transform: { experimentalImportSupport: true, inlineRequires: true } });` (keep experimentalImportSupport:true — it's Expo's default and required for the serializer reconcile path, see @expo/metro-config/build/serializer/reconcileTransformSerializerPlugin.js:171-173). Then restart Metro with cache clear (`npx expo start -c` via ensure-metro; stale transform cache is the known killer per rn-dev-iteration-flow memory). Behavior deltas to verify, not code to change: (a) push.ts's module-scope Notifications.setNotificationHandler (src/lib/push.ts:23-30) now runs at first ensurePushRegistration/requestPushPermission call (App.tsx:98 effect) instead of boot — still before any foreground notification can arrive post-login, acceptable, but re-test the foreground-banner path; (b) screen module eval moves from boot into first navigate() — this stacks with P2's startTransition/InteractionManager work (net win: boot pays nothing, first visit pays eval+mount inside the transition). Note explicitly in the implementation doc: this flip does NOT fix P8 — i18n/index.ts uses every imported JSON immediately in its module body (RESOURCES literal at :131-140), so those inlined requires still execute at i18n module-eval; the i18n restructure (separate finding) is still required.
findings.acceptance: With the boot HUD from the Release-recipe finding: cold-start time drops measurably in BOTH Debug and Release (expect hundreds of ms on-device; largest single lever in this dimension). Functional smoke: login, all 7 tabs, chat stream, language switch, foreground push banner, ambient toggle — all unchanged. `npm run type-check` green (no TS impact).
findings.risk: Modules relying on import-time side effects that are only imported via NAMED bindings get deferred — push.ts is the one identified instance (verified benign); if a regression surfaces, Metro supports `nonInlinedRequires` to exempt specific modules rather than reverting. Must clear Metro cache or the flag silently doesn't apply.

findings.title: P8 implementation: i18n static per-language require-map — init with en + device language only, lazy-load the other 6-7 languages on switch
findings.problem: src/i18n/index.ts eagerly imports 96 locale JSONs (8 languages × 12 namespaces, 563,535 bytes measured across packages/ui-kit/src/locales/*) and feeds all of them into i18n.init at module-eval — which App.tsx imports as a bare side-effect import before first render. A user only ever needs 2 languages at boot (en fallback + device/settings language); the other ~420-470KB of JSON→object materialization is pure wasted JS-thread time and retained heap on every cold start. dynamic import() is unavailable in this Hermes/Metro setup (documented at App.tsx:57-59, 'Requiring unknown module 4012'), so the fix must be a static-literal require map, which Metro resolves at build time and defers at run time.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/i18n/index.ts:18-113 — 96 static JSON imports; :131-140 — RESOURCES literal consumes all of them at module-eval (so even with inlineRequires:true they all execute); :156-165 — init({ lng: detectDeviceLanguage(), fallbackLng: 'en', resources: RESOURCES }); :171-175 — loadAndSwitchLanguage is already the single switch entry point and already async-signature-compatible with the web lazy version; src/i18n/useUiLanguageSync.ts:18 — the only runtime caller, already funnels through it. EN_RESOURCES (:116-129) is the t() type source via i18next.d.ts and must stay eagerly imported.
findings.fix: Rewrite src/i18n/index.ts: (1) KEEP the 12 en imports and EN_RESOURCES exactly as-is (type source + fallbackLng). (2) DELETE the 84 non-en imports and the RESOURCES literal. (3) Add a static loader map — one arrow function per language whose body contains 12 literal-path require() calls (Metro bundles them; execution deferred until the function is called): `const LOADERS: Record<Exclude<SupportedGenerationLanguage, 'en'>, () => Record<keyof typeof EN_RESOURCES, object>> = { 'zh-Hans': () => ({ account: require('../../../../packages/ui-kit/src/locales/zh-Hans/account.json'), ambient: require('.../ambient.json'), /* ...12 ns */ }), ja: () => ({...}), ko, es, fr, de, pt };` — require() with string literals is the pattern that works where import() fails. (4) Init with only what's needed: `const device = detectDeviceLanguage(); const resources: Record<string, unknown> = { en: EN_RESOURCES }; if (device !== 'en') resources[device] = LOADERS[device]();` then pass to init. (5) Rewrite loadAndSwitchLanguage: `if (lang !== 'en' && !i18n.hasResourceBundle(lang, 'common')) { const b = LOADERS[lang](); for (const [ns, res] of Object.entries(b)) i18n.addResourceBundle(lang, ns, res, true, true); } await i18n.changeLanguage(lang);` — this matches the web ui-web lazy-chunk semantics, so the '介质差异' header comment should be updated to say the RN medium is a static require map instead of 'all statically bundled'. Both callers (useUiLanguageSync, onboarding detectDeviceLanguage write-back) need zero changes.
findings.acceptance: `cd apps/mobile && npm run type-check` green (i18next.d.ts still keys off typeof EN_RESOURCES). On a device set to Japanese: UI boots in Japanese (loader ran at init). Switch settings.generationLanguage en→zh-Hans→en: all strings flip with no missing-key fallbacks (spot-check chat/tasks/profile namespaces). Boot HUD delta: measurable drop when device language is en (7 languages skipped). Heap: ~0.4-0.5MB less retained JSON objects (optional Instruments Allocations check).
findings.risk: Mechanical but wide (84 imports → 7 loader bodies) — a typo'd path fails at Metro build time, not runtime, so it's caught immediately. addResourceBundle deep/overwrite flags (true,true) must be passed or nested keys can shadow. No parity risk: web already lazy-loads non-en (ui-web import.meta.glob), this converges RN to the same behavior.

findings.title: lucide-react-native barrel: 64 import sites pull a 1,713-icon index — replace with one local deep-import shim
findings.problem: Every `import { X } from 'lucide-react-native'` resolves to dist/esm/lucide-react-native.mjs, a barrel that re-exports 1,713 icon modules (verified: 1,713 export lines / 3,428 files in dist/esm/icons). Metro does no tree shaking, so all 1,713 createLucideIcon module factories execute when the barrel is first required — today that's at boot (inlineRequires off); after the inlineRequires flip it's at the first lucide icon render (LoginScreen or first AppShell frame — still on the critical path to interactive). The app uses on the order of dozens of icons; ~1,650 modules are dead weight in both bundle size and one-shot eval time.
findings.evidence: grep: 64 files under apps/mobile/src import from 'lucide-react-native' (e.g. src/ui/Spinner.tsx:13 `import { Loader2 }`, src/screens/NowScreen.tsx, src/components/chat/*). node_modules/lucide-react-native/package.json exports map has only '.' and './icons' — and './icons' points at dist/esm/icons/index.mjs, ANOTHER all-icons barrel, so the official subpaths give no relief. dist/esm/lucide-react-native.mjs:8+ — one `export { default as X, default as XIcon, default as LucideX } from './icons/x.mjs'` line per icon, 1,713 of them. BootScreen itself hand-rolls its spinner (src/screens/BootScreen.tsx:55 comment, no lucide import), so with inlineRequires the barrel cost lands at the first real screen, not the boot spinner.
findings.fix: Create apps/mobile/src/ui/lucide.ts as the single icon gateway: for each icon actually used (collect via `grep -rhoE 'import \{[^}]+\} from "lucide-react-native"' apps/mobile/src | tr ',' '\n' | sort -u` — expect ~80-120 unique names), one line: `export { default as Loader2 } from 'lucide-react-native/dist/esm/icons/loader-2.mjs';` (kebab-case file names; numeric icons like Loader2→loader-2.mjs, watch aliases — if a name has no file, find it via `ls node_modules/lucide-react-native/dist/esm/icons | grep <fragment>`). Codemod the 64 import sites: `from "lucide-react-native"` → relative path to the shim (mechanical sed + type-check to catch misses). Metro note: these deep subpaths are NOT in the package's exports map — Metro's package-exports resolution is non-strict and falls back to file resolution with a warning; if this setup errors instead, extend the EXISTING resolveRequest hook in metro.config.js:22-31 with a clause mapping `lucide-react-native/dist/…` requests straight to the absolute file path (same pattern as the react-native redirect already there). Do this AFTER the inlineRequires flip and only if the measured first-icon-render cost or bundle-size win justifies it — mechanism is confirmed, magnitude (est. 100-300ms eval + ~1-1.5MB bundle) is estimated.
filesToTouch: apps/mobile/src/**（64 个 lucide import 站点，grep 清单为准）
findings.acceptance: `npm run type-check` green; `npx expo export --platform ios` bundle size drops ~1MB+ vs before; all icons render identically on device (visual spot-check of chat toolbar, tabs, settings rows — owner verdict per skill workflow). No Metro resolution errors in .rn-metro.log (a fallback WARNING per deep path is acceptable).
findings.risk: lucide upgrades can rename dist files — breakage is at Metro build time (loud, not silent). The 64-file codemod is churn-heavy; keep it a dedicated commit. proactive-ai-frontend (web) uses lucide-react with Vite tree-shaking and needs no change — no parity concern.

findings.title: Sign-in effect fires 4 async chains in the same tick as AppShell first mount — stagger the two non-urgent ones
findings.problem: On auth ready, App.tsx's user-effect synchronously kicks startSync (SQLite scheduler), ensureDevice({forceRefresh:true}) (network POST), ensurePushRegistration (permissions query + possible token registration → network), and resumeAmbientIfEnabled (AsyncStorage read + possible source startup) — in the exact same tick React is mounting AppShell, which itself fires the usePipeline/useComposio/cards fetch burst (P5 baseline). The JSON parsing and state updates from these responses all land inside the first-interactive window, competing with first-frame work on the JS thread.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:88-101 — single useEffect([user?.id]) calling all four; :140 — AppShell mounts in the same render pass once settings gate passes. ensureDevice/ensurePushRegistration are pure background bookkeeping (device row refresh, silent token re-report — push.ts:5-16 states registration re-runs next launch anyway on failure); neither affects anything the user sees at boot. startSync and resumeAmbientIfEnabled have continuity semantics (local history, ambient capture) and should stay immediate.
findings.fix: In the same effect, wrap the two non-urgent calls: `const task = InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions(() => { void ensureDevice(user.id, { forceRefresh: true }).catch(err => console.warn('[devices] registration failed after sign-in', err)); void ensurePushRegistration(user.id); }); return () => task.cancel();` (import InteractionManager from react-native; keep startSync + resumeAmbientIfEnabled where they are). This pushes them past the shell's mount/animation frames without changing any semantics — both are idempotent and already fire-and-forget.
findings.acceptance: After login on device: device row still refreshes (check pai devices list / backend log shows the register call ~1-2s later than before) and push token still reports when OS-granted; no functional change. First-frame-to-interactive after login feels no worse and profiler (Debug) shows the two fetches scheduled after interactions.
findings.risk: Negligible — worst case the device-row refresh happens a second later; the push chain explicitly self-heals next launch (push.ts header comment). Cleanup of the InteractionManager handle on user change avoids firing for a signed-out user.

findings.title: Closed card chat stays mounted forever with 2 live SSE connections (zombie ChatScreen)
findings.problem: CardChatScreen latches the last opened card (`lastTarget`) so exit animation can render one more frame, but never clears it: after the sheet closes, `shown = target ?? lastTarget.current` keeps rendering the FULL ChatScreen for that card off-screen, permanently. That ChatScreen's Conversation component unconditionally runs useConversationRuntime (persistent /conversation/stream SSE + reconnect/backoff loop) and useBrowserPanel → useBrowserSession (a second persistent /browser/events SSE with an infinite while-loop reconnect every 1.5s). So closing a card chat leaves 2 zombie network streams + reducers + reconnect timers running for the rest of the app session, on top of the main chat's own 2 streams — radio wakeups, JSON parsing, and server connections for a screen the user exited.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/screens/CardChatScreen.tsx:110-113 (`const lastTarget = useRef(...); if (target) lastTarget.current = target; const shown = target ?? lastTarget.current;`) and :167-177 (renders <ChatScreen kind="card" ...> whenever `card` non-null — which is forever after first open). ChatScreen.tsx:393-406 mounts useConversationRuntime unconditionally (no `open` gating); ChatScreen.tsx:412 mounts useBrowserPanel. packages/state/src/queries/conversation.ts:232-398 (SSE + reconnect loop lives for hook lifetime); packages/state/src/queries/browser-session.ts:83-125 (while(!cancelled) SSE loop, RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS=1500, runs for hook lifetime). AppShell.tsx:275 keeps <CardChatScreen target={cardChat}> in the tree with target=null after close.
findings.fix: Unmount the sheet content after the exit animation completes, mirroring the KeepAlivePage pattern (components/app/KeepAlivePage.tsx:34-43): add `const [contentShown, setContentShown] = useState(false)`; in the open/close effect (CardChatScreen.tsx:123-128), on open set contentShown=true; on close use the withTiming completion callback `withTiming(height, {...}, (finished) => { if (finished) runOnJS(setContentShown)(false); })` and additionally clear `lastTarget.current = null` inside the same callback. Render `{card && contentShown ? (<>…ChatScreen…</>) : null}`. Keep `pointerEvents` logic unchanged. This keeps the 500ms exit frame intact (contentShown stays true during the animation) while guaranteeing the ChatScreen (and both SSE hooks) unmount ~500ms after close.
findings.acceptance: Open a card chat, close it, wait 1s. Verify via Metro console (add temporary log in useBrowserSession connect() and conversation.ts connect()) that no new /browser/events or /conversation/stream requests fire for the card's thread after close, and the existing ones abort (cleanup logs 'closed'). Exit animation still plays without content flashing empty. Reopening the same or another card works.
findings.risk: If contentShown flips false before the 500ms timing finishes (e.g. rapid reopen), guard by only clearing when target is still null. Web CardChatOverlay uses the same lastTarget trick but unmounts via AnimatePresence — this change restores parity with web's actual unmount behavior, not a divergence.

findings.title: useAmbientLiveSession polls up to 10,000-row SQLite queries every 5s while Ambient page is hidden
findings.problem: The live-session effect runs whenever ambientOn is true, with no pageActive or AppState gating. Every 5 seconds it executes store.listCandidateWindows({limit: 10_000}) + store.listRawEvents({sourceType:'transcript', eventType:'transcript.ready', limit: 10_000}) + 6 more per-source listRawEvents queries, then setState×3 → re-render of the keep-alive-mounted AmbientScreen even when the user is on another tab. Because the queries fetch ALL of today's windows/transcripts, cost grows linearly through the day for an all-day ambient user — by evening this is hundreds of rows deserialized every 5s, all day, mostly while the screen is invisible. This is the single biggest recurring background JS cost when ambient is on.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientLiveSession.ts:67 (LIVE_SESSION_TODAY_LIMIT = 10_000), :96-140 (effect gated only on `ambientOn`; interval = setInterval(refreshWindows, 5000)), :112-121 (the three parallel store reads). Consumer: apps/mobile/src/screens/AmbientScreen.tsx:202-203 — AmbientScreen is keep-alive mounted (AppShell KeepAlivePage), so the hook lives forever after first Ambient visit. Contrast with components/ambient/AmbientTimelineSummaryStatusPanel.tsx:152-158 which already gates its identical 5s poll on usePageActive.
findings.fix: 1) Add an `active: boolean` option to UseAmbientLiveSessionOptions; in AmbientScreen pass `active: pageActive` (usePageActive() is already imported there at :56/:812 — hoist the call above the hook usage). 2) Change the poll effect dep/guard at useAmbientLiveSession.ts:96-140 from `if (!ambientOn)` to `if (!ambientOn || !active)` (keep clearing state only on !ambientOn; on !active just stop polling so switch-back is instant with stale data + immediate refreshWindows on reactivation). 3) Keep the subscribeAmbientLiveTranscript push subscription (it's cheap and event-driven). 4) Separately cut LIVE_SESSION_TODAY_LIMIT for the polled path: liveSessionDataToSession only needs today's recent windows — cap transcripts to the last N (e.g. 200, order desc + reverse) or track a `since` cursor of the last seen rawEvent id and merge incrementally.
findings.acceptance: Add a temporary console.count in refreshWindows. With ambient on: on Ambient tab it fires every 5s; switch to NOW/Chat tab → zero fires; switch back → one immediate fire then 5s cadence. Live session card still updates in real time via the native transcript listener while on-page.
findings.risk: The NOW screen does not consume this hook (verified — only AmbientScreen:203), so gating on Ambient's pageActive loses nothing. If a future NOW live card consumes it, it must pass its own active flag. dev/web has no keep-alive equivalent, so no parity concern.

findings.title: useAmbientTimeline polls SQLite (~9 queries) every 5s forever once Ambient visited, even with ambient off and page hidden
findings.problem: The timeline hook's 5s interval has no gating at all — not on pageActive, not on ambient enabled, not on AppState. It runs store.listTimelineEvents + listCandidateWindows + 7 per-source listRawEvents queries, then 4 setStates → full re-render of the hidden keep-alive AmbientScreen (whose timeline rows are the expensive GlassCard stacks from baseline P4) every 5 seconds for the rest of the session, even for a user who turned ambient off.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientTimeline.ts:90-96 (useEffect: `const interval = setInterval(() => void load(), 5_000)` unconditional), :46-80 (load = 3 awaited store calls, loadLatestRawEvents at :114-134 fans out 7 more queries), consumer apps/mobile/src/screens/AmbientScreen.tsx:177-187 (top-level of keep-alive screen). usePageActive exists and is already used elsewhere in the same screen (AmbientScreen.tsx:812).
findings.fix: Add `active = true` parameter to useAmbientTimeline (signature: `useAmbientTimeline(localDate = todayLocalDate(), active = true)`); in the effect at :90-96, `if (!active) return;` before starting (still run one `load()` when becoming active so switch-back repaints fresh, mirroring AmbientTimelineSummaryStatusPanel.tsx:152-158). In AmbientScreen pass `useAmbientTimeline(todayLocalDate(), pageActive)` — hoist the existing usePageActive() call above :187. Optionally also skip polling while ambient is off AND storeStatus shows no writes, but page gating alone removes ~100% of the hidden-page cost.
findings.acceptance: console.count in load(): fires every 5s only while Ambient tab is the active page; zero fires on other tabs; one immediate fire on tab return. Timeline still picks up new entries within 5s while viewing.
findings.risk: Dismiss action calls load() directly (:82-88) — unaffected. dev web unmounts the view on tab switch so this matches dev's effective behavior.

findings.title: Every mounted chat opens a permanent /browser/events SSE with fixed 1.5s reconnect, even when no browser session ever exists
findings.problem: useBrowserSession starts its SSE loop unconditionally for the hook's lifetime. The keep-alive main ChatScreen therefore holds a second permanent SSE connection (besides /conversation/stream) from first chat visit until sign-out, even though 99% of sessions never use the browser tool. Worse, the reconnect loop retries at a FIXED 1500ms with no exponential backoff and no cap: if the endpoint errors persistently (backend deploy, 5xx, auth hiccup), the app hammers the server every 1.5s indefinitely — a battery and server-load hazard. Combined with the CardChatScreen zombie (separate finding) this multiplies to N permanent browser-event streams.
findings.evidence: packages/state/src/queries/browser-session.ts:83-125 — `while (!cancelled)` loop, `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS))` with constant RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS=1500 (:46); no session-existence gate, no backoff growth. Consumer: apps/mobile/src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx:412 (useBrowserPanel(threadId) → useBrowserSession) inside the keep-alive Conversation. Contrast: conversation.ts:382-387 does exponential backoff (RECONNECT_BASE_MS * 2**(attempt-1) capped).
findings.fix: Two independent changes in packages/state/src/queries/browser-session.ts: (a) add exponential backoff mirroring conversation.ts — track `attempt`, reset to 0 after a successful read of at least one chunk, delay = min(1500 * 2**attempt, 30_000); (b) gate the connection on need: add an optional `active?: boolean` param (default true to preserve web behavior); RN's useBrowserPanel passes `busy || session != null` from the conversation runtime (browser sessions are only ever created mid-turn by browser_tool, so connecting while a turn is in flight cannot miss browser:opened). Keep the session-close→reconnect semantics unchanged. When gating flips false with a live session, keep it connected (session != null keeps it true) — only never-used chats skip the stream.
findings.acceptance: Backoff: kill the backend locally / point at a 500ing endpoint and confirm reconnect logs space out 1.5s→3s→6s… capped. Gating: open chat, send no message → no /browser/events request in server logs; send a message that triggers browser_tool → panel entry appears (browser:opened received). Web (proactive-ai-frontend, apps/web) type-checks and browser panel still works with default param.
findings.risk: This hook is shared with web (packages/state) — parity-sensitive. Default `active=true` keeps web byte-identical; only RN opts into gating. The gating premise (sessions only created during a running turn) should be re-verified against backend browser session creation paths before shipping; if a session can appear while idle, fall back to backoff-only (still worth it).

findings.title: SSE generators never cancel the reader on early exit — resync/break paths strand open HTTP streams
findings.problem: proxySSE and proxyGetSSE only call reader.releaseLock() in their finally blocks, never reader.cancel(). When a consumer exits the for-await loop without aborting the fetch — which the conversation loop does on every `conversation:resync` frame (plain `break`, signal NOT aborted) — the generator's finally releases the lock but leaves the underlying expo/fetch body stream open. The old connection dangles (server keeps it alive with pings; client keeps buffering) while the loop immediately opens a NEW stream, so each server-side resync leaks one connection until the server times it out. Same latent hazard for any future early-break consumer.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/transport/sse.ts:44-46 and :97-99 (finally { reader.releaseLock(); } — no cancel). Early-exit consumer: packages/state/src/queries/conversation.ts:361-364 (`if (event.type === "conversation:resync") { lastEventIdRef.current = null; break; }`) — the surrounding AbortController is only aborted by the effect cleanup (:392-397), and connect() then reassigns `abort = new AbortController()` (:253) for the next connection without aborting the previous one, so nothing ever closes the resync'd stream.
findings.fix: In both generators' finally blocks replace `reader.releaseLock()` with: `try { await reader.cancel(); } catch { /* already closed */ } finally { reader.releaseLock(); }` (reader.cancel is the standard way to signal no-more-reads and tear down the connection; it is a no-op after clean EOF). Additionally, harden conversation.ts: in connect(), before `abort = new AbortController()` at :253, call `abort?.abort()` so any previous cycle's connection is definitively dead when a new one starts (belt-and-braces for the resync path).
findings.acceptance: packages/core transport tests still pass (`npm run check:packages`); add a unit test in transport.test.ts asserting the mock reader's cancel() is called when the generator is returned early (generator.return()). Manual: trigger a resync (or simulate by yielding a conversation:resync event) and confirm the old response body's cancel fires (mock/spy).
findings.risk: Shared with all three web apps — reader.cancel() on an already-errored/done stream must be swallowed (the try/catch does). Some fetch polyfills reject cancel() after releaseLock — order matters: cancel BEFORE releaseLock.

findings.title: Ambient timeline SQLite + live-transcript memory store are device-global and never cleared on sign-out (cross-account data exposure)
findings.problem: The ambient timeline store is a module singleton over a fixed database name 'ambient_timeline' with no per-user scoping (unlike the sync engine, which uses pinai_sync_${userId}), and its readers (useAmbientTimeline, useAmbientLiveSession, summary panels) query by localDate only — no owner filter. performSignOut sweeps AsyncStorage and stops runtimes but never touches this SQLite DB or the in-memory live-transcript store. Result: after an in-process account switch, user B's Ambient tab renders user A's transcripts, locations, and health events — the most sensitive data in the app. (The upload outbox is safe: outbox.pending() filters by ownerUserId.)
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/ambient/timeline/store.ts:11-18 (singleton, createExpoDatabase("ambient_timeline"), no user in name); contrast apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/sync-bootstrap.ts:32 (per-user DB name). apps/mobile/src/lib/sign-out.ts:47-83 — cleanup list is stopSync, stopAmbient, sweepAsyncStorage (AsyncStorage prefixes only, :30-40), runSignOutCleanups, supabase.signOut, queryClient.clear — nothing wipes ambient_timeline or live-transcript-store. apps/mobile/src/ambient/live/live-transcript-store.ts (module-level `history`/current state, grep confirms no reset/clear export). Callers already have userId in scope at start time (runtime owns runtimeOwnerUserId); read-side hooks can get it from a module setter invoked in startIngestLoop/reconcile, or accept the simpler alternative: keep one DB but add a wipeAllTables() on the store (core SqliteTimelineStore) invoked from performSignOut before sweepAsyncStorage. Also export clearAmbientLiveTranscript() from live-transcript-store (reset current + history) and call it in performSignOut. Note the ingest outbox DB ('ambient') can stay shared — it is owner-filtered.
filesToTouch: packages/core/src/sync (SqliteTimelineStore — only if wipe method chosen)
findings.acceptance: Sign in as A with ambient on, generate timeline events; sign out; sign in as B (dev-auth or second account): Ambient tab shows an empty timeline and empty live history. Sign back in as A: with per-user DB, A's history is preserved (per-user variant) or empty (wipe variant — acceptable, distilled data was already uploaded).
