Wipe variant loses local-only raw events that were never uploaded by design — that is the privacy-correct behavior on sign-out but should be stated in the PR.

findings.title: Push registration latch never resets on sign-out — next account gets no APNs token
findings.problem: push.ts guards token registration with a module-level `registered` boolean that is set true once and never reset. performSignOut clears device credentials but not this latch. On an in-process account switch, App.tsx re-runs ensureDevice(forceRefresh) creating a fresh device row for user B, but ensurePushRegistration() returns immediately (registered===true), so the new device row never gets the APNs token PUT — user B receives no push notifications until the app is killed and relaunched.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:39 (`let registered = false`), :42-43 (`if (registered) return`), :72-73 (same guard in ensurePushRegistration); no reset anywhere (grep). Sign-out cleanup chain registers only clearDeviceCredentials: apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:52, lib/sign-out.ts:60-65. Post-switch registration entry: App.tsx:96-98 calls ensurePushRegistration(user.id) on the new user — no-ops.
findings.fix: Export `function resetPushRegistration(): void { registered = false; }` from lib/push.ts and register it in the sign-out chain — simplest is inside push.ts itself at module scope: `registerSignOutCleanup(() => { registered = false; })` (import registerSignOutCleanup from @pin-ai/core, same mechanism App.tsx uses at :52), keeping the latch and its reset in one file.
findings.acceptance: Sign in (push granted) → console shows '[push] APNs token registered device=X'. Sign out, sign in as another (or same) account without killing the app → the log line appears again with the new device id. Backend pai device row for the second session has push token set.
findings.risk: None meaningful — registerToken is idempotent server-side (PUT). Ensure the import doesn't create a require cycle (core is a leaf; safe).

findings.title: stopIngestLoop keeps ownerUserId and fires an un-awaited final flush — sign-out races credential cleanup and can resurrect device creds
findings.problem: stopIngestLoop() (called from stopAmbient during sign-out) clears the 30s timer but (a) never nulls ownerUserId and (b) fires `void flushSignals()` fire-and-forget. performSignOut then proceeds to sweepAsyncStorage and clearDeviceCredentials while that flush is still running. flushSignals→ensureDevice(owner) reads SecureStore: if the sweep already deleted creds, ensureDevice calls registerDevice — POST /devices/register with the still-valid JWT (supabase.auth.signOut runs later) — creating a ghost device row for the signed-out user AND re-writing deviceId/deviceToken/owner into SecureStore AFTER clearDeviceCredentials ran, leaving stale keychain creds bound to the old account. Even the benign interleaving uploads the user's ambient signals after they pressed Sign Out. Because ownerUserId survives, any later stray flushSignals/refreshOutboxCount call also still acts on the old owner.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/ambient/ingest.ts:219-223 (stopIngestLoop: clearInterval; `void flushSignals();` — ownerUserId untouched), :104-107 (flushSignals gates on ownerUserId, uses it as owner), :133 (ensureDevice(owner) inside flush). apps/mobile/src/lib/devices.ts:45-56 (registerDevice writes SecureStore), :93-101 (clearDeviceCredentials). Ordering: apps/mobile/src/lib/sign-out.ts:50-65 (stopSync → await stopAmbient → sweepAsyncStorage → runSignOutCleanups[clearDeviceCredentials] → supabase.signOut). stopAmbient → stopIngestLoop at ambient/runtime.ts:261.
findings.fix: Split shutdown semantics in ingest.ts: `export async function stopIngestLoop(opts: { finalFlush?: boolean } = {}): Promise<void> { if (timer) clearInterval(timer); timer = null; if (opts.finalFlush) await flushSignals(); ownerUserId = null; setOutboxPending(0); }`. In ambient/runtime.ts: stopAmbient() calls `await stopIngestLoop({ finalFlush: true })` (preserves today's last-drain semantics for the normal toggle-off path but now awaited and followed by owner reset); the AppState background handler keeps calling flushSignals directly (unchanged). performSignOut ordering then guarantees the final flush completes (with valid creds+JWT) BEFORE sweepAsyncStorage/clearDeviceCredentials run — no ghost registration, and post-sign-out flush calls no-op because ownerUserId is null.
findings.acceptance: Instrument devices.ts registerDevice with a log; sign out while ambient is on with pending outbox items: no '/devices/register' fires during/after sign-out, SecureStore holds no device keys afterwards (add a debug read), and the final batch either uploads before credentials are cleared or stays in the outbox (still owner-tagged, filtered out for the next user). startAmbient after re-login re-establishes ownerUserId and flushes normally.
findings.risk: startAmbientSources' failure path (runtime.ts:239-244) also calls stopIngestLoop — becomes await-able; enqueue order there is safe. reconcileEnabledSources(:373) same. Make both call sites `await` or keep `void` deliberately with a comment (they're not on the sign-out path).

findings.title: Native live-transcript bridge listeners are attached once and never removed (survive ambient-off and sign-out)
findings.problem: ensureNativeLiveTranscriptBridge attaches 6 AmbientAudio native event listeners the first time any consumer renders with ambientOn=true, stores the handle in module state, and nothing in the codebase ever calls handle.remove(). The listeners persist after ambient is disabled and after sign-out, continuing to funnel any native audio events into the module-level live-transcript store. Cost is near-zero while capture is stopped (native emits nothing), but it is an unbounded-lifetime subscription that also feeds the cross-account store issue, and if ambient is re-enabled by a different account before reconcile completes, events land in a store the previous account's UI state still references.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/hooks/useAmbientLiveSession.ts:57-58 (module-level nativeLiveBridgeStarted/nativeLiveBridgeHandle), :91-94 (effect only ever calls ensureNativeLiveTranscriptBridge, no cleanup), :241-250 (handle stored, remove never invoked — grep confirms no other reference). Listener fan-out: apps/mobile/src/ambient/live/transcript-listener.ts:49-77.
findings.fix: Refcount the bridge: in useAmbientLiveSession, replace ensureNativeLiveTranscriptBridge() with acquire/release — `useEffect(() => { if (!ambientOn) return; const release = acquireNativeLiveTranscriptBridge(); return release; }, [ambientOn])`; implement acquire to addListeners on 0→1 and remove() on 1→0 (keep the try/catch degradation for unlinked native builds). Alternatively (simpler): export releaseNativeLiveTranscriptBridge() and call it from performSignOut alongside the live-store clear.
findings.acceptance: Toggle ambient on → off: temporary log in transcript-listener remove() fires; toggle on again: listeners re-attach and live card still streams transcripts. Sign-out with ambient on: remove() fires as part of cleanup.
findings.risk: Rapid ambientOn flapping must not double-attach — the refcount plus the existing started-guard covers it. Verify Expo EventSubscription.remove() is idempotent (it is).

findings.title: Device-timeline photos render full-resolution via RN <Image> with cache-busting signed URLs — migrate remote images to expo-image
findings.problem: expo-image is NOT installed (apps/mobile/package.json has no expo-image entry). All remote images go through core RN <Image>, which on iOS decodes the source bitmap at FULL resolution regardless of view size. The worst case is the device timeline: pai signal media are user photos from Supabase Storage (often 12MP, ~4000x3000 → ~45MB RGBA per decode) rendered into a width:100% x height:320 container. The rows live in a non-virtualized .map list (baseline P4), so several photos can be decoded and retained simultaneously → tens-to-hundreds of MB. Additionally, the image URI is a signed URL minted per mount (useDeviceMediaUrl → deviceMediaUrl), so the query-string token changes every time → RN's URI-keyed cache misses on every remount and re-downloads/re-decodes. Favicons (WorkGroup) and connector bitmap logos (DataConnections) also use RN <Image> with no persistent disk cache guarantee.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/connect/DeviceTimeline.tsx:344 `<Image source={{ uri: mediaUrl }} style={styles.media} resizeMode="contain" />` with styles.media at :481 `{ width: "100%", height: 320 }`; signed URL from useDeviceMediaUrl at :244-260 calling deviceMediaUrl (packages/core/src/api/devices.ts:158); rows rendered via `.map` at DeviceTimeline.tsx:212. WorkGroup.tsx:104 `<Image source={{ uri: icon }} style={styles.linkFavicon} />` (14x14, google s2 favicon, :71-77). DataConnections.tsx:299-303 `<Image source={{ uri: logo }} style={styles.iconLogo} .../>` (20x20 bitmap logos). `grep expo-image apps/mobile/package.json` → no hit.
findings.fix: 1) `npx expo install expo-image` in apps/mobile (then re-run pod install via the device build script). 2) DeviceTimeline.tsx:344 — replace RN Image with `import { Image } from "expo-image"`; props: `source={{ uri: mediaUrl }}`, `contentFit="contain"`, `cachePolicy="disk"`, and critically `recyclingKey={filePath}` plus `source={{ uri: mediaUrl, cacheKey: filePath }}` — using the stable storage_path as cacheKey so signed-URL token churn no longer busts the cache. expo-image's allowDownscaling (default true) caps decode near the 320pt view size instead of full 12MP. Do the same for TimelineVideo poster if added later. 3) WorkGroup.tsx:104 — swap to expo-image with `cachePolicy="disk"` (favicon URL is stable, no cacheKey needed). 4) DataConnections.tsx:299 bitmap branch — swap to expo-image, `cachePolicy="disk"`. Keep the SvgLogo branch as-is (separate finding). Do NOT touch bundled-asset <Image> call sites in this step (AuroraBackground/ProfileScreen goal images are require()'d; separate findings).
findings.acceptance: Open Connect → device timeline with ≥5 photo signals on device: Xcode memory gauge drops by tens of MB vs before (measure both). Leave the page, return: images appear instantly with no re-download (verify via Network inspector / airplane-mode revisit shows cached photos). Favicons/connector logos render after a cold restart with radio off (disk cache hit). `npm run type-check` passes.
findings.risk: expo-image is the Expo-blessed standard, low risk. Visual parity: contentFit="contain" matches resizeMode="contain"; borderRadius on style still applies. proactive-ai-frontend unaffected (web uses natively). One check: expo-image needs a New-Arch-compatible version pin matching SDK (expo install handles it).

findings.title: @shopify/react-native-skia (~85MB static libs) is linked solely to draw a static, draw-once background — replace AuroraBackground's Canvas with a baked image and drop the dependency
findings.problem: After the earlier heat fix, AuroraBackground became fully static: 6 fixed radial-gradient spots drawn once on a full-screen Skia Canvas. That Canvas is the ONLY Skia usage left in the entire app, yet it costs: (a) the whole Skia native library linked into the binary (libskia.a 35MB + libsvg.a 11MB + skottie/sksg/skshaper etc. ≈ 85MB of static libs; several MB of final binary + slower builds); (b) one screen-sized persistent GPU surface per mounted instance (~1179x2556x4 ≈ 12MB at 3x) — and ChatSheet is ALWAYS mounted (keep-alive for SSE) with its own AuroraBackground, plus CardChatScreen mounts a second one when open, plus LoginScreen a third pre-auth. A static picture rendered by a GPU canvas runtime is pure overhead.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/ui/AuroraBackground.tsx:17 imports @shopify/react-native-skia; :69-73 `<Canvas style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}>` drawing static SPOTS (:23-30, no animation — header comment :1-14 documents the deliberate static design). `grep -rln react-native-skia src` → only src/ui/AuroraBackground.tsx. Mount sites: src/components/app/ChatSheet.tsx:59 (always mounted — ChatSheet.tsx:2-3 '常 mount…保住在流 SSE'), src/screens/CardChatScreen.tsx:141, src/screens/LoginScreen.tsx:125. Lib sizes measured: ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/XCFrameworkIntermediates/react-native-skia/ → libskia.a 35,444,664 B, libsvg.a 10,971,440 B, libskshaper.a 13.5MB, libskottie.a 12.6MB, libsksg.a 10.1MB. package.json:28 "@shopify/react-native-skia": "2.6.2".
findings.fix: 1) Pre-render the 6 SPOTS radial gradients once into a transparent-alpha WebP (e.g. 780x1688 ≈ half of 3x screen; the gradients are soft so upscaling is invisible). Generation options: a one-off Node script with `sharp`/`canvas`, or an HTML file reproducing each `radial-gradient(ellipse rx ry at cx cy, color 0%, transparent 60%)` from SPOTS and screenshotting — commit the output as src/assets/aurora-spots.webp. 2) In AuroraBackground.tsx replace the `<Canvas>` block (:69-73) and SkiaSpot (:33-49) with `<Image source={require("../assets/aurora-spots.webp")} style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} resizeMode="cover" />` (keep the base bg-gradient.jpg layer :63-67, children slot, and veil :75 unchanged — layer order preserved for LoginScreen's nebula video). 3) `npm uninstall @shopify/react-native-skia` in apps/mobile, prebuild/pod install, confirm no other import breaks (grep already confirms none). AuroraBackground.web.tsx is separate and untouched.

Side-by-side screenshots of ChatSheet, CardChatScreen, LoginScreen vs current build are visually indistinguishable (owner verifies on device per pixel-parity rule). Xcode memory gauge with ChatSheet open drops ~10-25MB (two fewer live GPU surfaces).

Keep the generation script checked in so colors can be retuned. Web端 (AuroraBackground.web.tsx) and proactive-ai-frontend are unaffected.

findings.title: Six 1024x1024 goal PNGs (1.57MB bundle, ~25MB decoded RAM) render into ≤96pt containers — downscale to 512px and recompress
findings.problem: All six goal illustrations are 1024x1024 PNGs (158-372KB each, 1.57MB total). Their largest render target is the Mirror grid image area: height 96pt area with image height 60-82pt (and 32x32pt in the detail sheet header) — ~245px tall at 3x. RN <Image> decodes bundled PNGs at full source resolution: 1024x1024x4B ≈ 4.2MB RGBA each, ~25MB for the six-card grid. ProfileScreen is a keep-alive screen (baseline architecture), so once the Mirror tab is visited that ~25MB stays resident for the session. The bundle also carries ~1.3MB of unnecessary pixels.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/profile/mirror-helpers.ts:78-85 require() the six PNGs; `sips -g pixelWidth` → all 1024x1024; `ls -l src/assets/goals/` → 158,179–371,519 B each (1,533,108 B total). Render sizes: ProfileScreen.tsx:403 `imgHeight = 96*0.62 or 96*0.85` (≤82pt), :417-421 `<Image source={visual.image} style={{ width: "100%", height: imgHeight }} resizeMode="contain" />`, :943 goalImageArea height 96; GoalDetailSheet.tsx:194 + :313 `headerImage: { width: 32, height: 32 }`.
findings.fix: Batch-resize the assets in place: `cd apps/mobile/src/assets/goals && for f in *.png; do sips -Z 512 "$f"; done` (512px = 2x headroom over the ~245px max render), then recompress with `npx @squoosh/cli` or pngquant (`pngquant --quality=70-90 --ext .png --force *.png`). Optionally convert to WebP (`sips -s format webp` or cwebp -q 82) and update the six require() extensions in mirror-helpers.ts:78-85 — WebP typically lands ~30-60KB per image. No code changes needed if staying PNG (same paths).
findings.acceptance: `ls -l src/assets/goals` total < 400KB (from 1.53MB). Xcode memory gauge after opening Profile → Mirror grid drops ~15-19MB vs before. Goal cards and detail sheet look identical on device at normal viewing (owner visual check — resizeMode contain, 512px @ ≤82pt render has 2x headroom).
findings.risk: Negligible; keep originals in git history in case a future screen renders them larger. If converting to WebP, verify Metro bundles .webp (supported by default assetExts).

findings.title: constellation-bg.mp4 is 3.87MB (68% of src/assets) at 1.54Mbps H.264 for a background that plays under a 70% white veil — re-encode to HEVC at ~500kbps
findings.problem: The shell background video is 640x1424 H.264 @ ~1.54Mbps, 20s → 3,878,826 B, the single largest asset in the app. It is only ever seen (a) under a rgba(255,255,255,0.7) veil at 0.5x speed in VideoBackdrop, and (b) at opacity 0.75 above the aurora in LoginScreen. Under that much attenuation, 1.54Mbps H.264 is far past visual saturation; HEVC at 400-600kbps is indistinguishable. This is pure bundle weight plus marginally higher decode bandwidth. (Playback-always-on is a deliberate owner decision — '根视频故意留' — so do NOT add pause gating; this is an asset-level fix only.)
findings.evidence: ffprobe: src/assets/constellation-bg.mp4 → h264, 640x1424, 20.08s, bit_rate 1,542,255. File 3,878,826 B (`ls -l src/assets`). Consumers: src/ui/VideoBackdrop.tsx:11 (require) with white/70 veil at :32/:39 and playbackRate 0.5 at :17; src/screens/LoginScreen.tsx:43 (same file) faded to 0.75 opacity. sphere.mp4 (720x720, 378kbps, 239KB, AiSphere.tsx:14) is already well-sized — leave it.
findings.fix: Re-encode once and replace in place: `ffmpeg -i constellation-bg.mp4 -c:v libx265 -tag:v hvc1 -crf 30 -preset slow -an constellation-bg.mp4.new && mv constellation-bg.mp4.new constellation-bg.mp4` (hvc1 tag required for iOS playback; -an strips the audio track if present). Target ≤1.2MB. iOS 17 deployment target (app.json expo-build-properties) guarantees hardware HEVC decode. If HEVC looks off under the veil, fall back to `-c:v libx264 -crf 28` (~1.8MB). No code changes.
findings.acceptance: File size ≤1.2MB (from 3.87MB); `ffprobe` shows hevc/hvc1. On device: shell background and login nebula look identical (owner check), loop is seamless, no decode stutter at 0.5x rate.
findings.risk: HEVC-in-expo-video on iOS is standard; only pitfall is forgetting the hvc1 tag (video renders black). Loop point must stay clean — verify first/last frame unchanged. Android is out of scope (iOS-only app today) but HEVC support there is API 21+ anyway.

findings.title: Connector SVG logos: in-memory-only XML cache refetches every cold start and SvgCss re-parses per row mount in a non-virtualized catalog
findings.problem: SvgLogo fetches each logos.composio.dev SVG as text, normalizes percent-rgb colors, and renders via SvgCss. The dedupe cache (svgXmlCache) is a module-level Map of Promises — it dies with the JS context, so every app launch refetches every visible logo over the network (catalog can mount dozens of rows at once since the list is non-virtualized per baseline P4), and each row mount pays an XML→tree parse in SvgCss plus a react-native-svg native node tree per 20x20 icon. There is no offline rendering of logos at all.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/connect/DataConnections.tsx:235-250 module-level `svgXmlCache = new Map<string, Promise<string>>()` + fetchSvgXml (no persistence); :254-273 SvgLogo useEffect fetch → `<SvgCss xml={xml} width={20} height={20} />`; :214-217 isSvgLogo (all composio logos are SVG); :194 logo URL builder. Catalog rows mount en masse via the non-virtualized DataConnections list (ConnectScreen.tsx:120, baseline P4).
findings.fix: Two-tier fix, keep the proven SvgCss render path (the percent-rgb normalization at :219-233 exists because expo-image/SDWebImage SVG rasterization was NOT validated against these logos — do not swap renderers blind). 1) Persist the normalized XML: back svgXmlCache with AsyncStorage (`@react-native-async-storage/async-storage`, already a transitive/workspace dep — verify, else expo install) under key `svg-logo:<uri>`; on fetchSvgXml, try storage first, write-through after normalize. SVGs are 1-10KB text; cap at ~200 entries, no eviction complexity needed. 2) Memoize the component: wrap SvgLogo in React.memo and hoist the parsed render by keying on xml (SvgCss already useMemo's parse per instance; memo prevents re-parse on parent re-renders — relevant because DataConnections re-renders on every connections poll). Acceptance-relevant only after P4's list virtualization lands; do this after P4.
findings.acceptance: Cold-start the app in airplane mode after one online visit to Connect: previously-seen connector logos render (from persisted XML) instead of falling back to lucide icons. Network inspector on second launch shows zero logos.composio.dev requests for cached logos.
findings.risk: Stale logo if composio redesigns an icon — acceptable (bust by including a cache version prefix in the storage key). Do not attempt the expo-image SVG route without device-verifying the outlook percent-rgb gradient case documented at :219-222.

findings.title: Fonts: no double-loading (question answered), but 8 weights load async via JS at every launch — optional native embedding
findings.problem: The suspected duplication does NOT exist: app.json lists the `expo-font` config plugin with NO fonts config (plugins array, bare string entry), so nothing is embedded natively; the only load path is useFonts in App.tsx pulling 4 Inter (~343KB each) + 4 Geist (~91KB each) ≈ 1.74MB of TTFs registered asynchronously on the JS thread at every cold start. Until resolution, text renders in the system font then swaps (deliberately not gating first paint — baseline verified). The improvement available is eliminating the async registration + font-swap frame entirely by embedding via the expo-font config plugin — but all styles reference Google-Fonts-style names (`fontFamily: "Inter_400Regular"`, 277 occurrences; 651 total fontFamily usages), and natively-embedded fonts are addressed by PostScript name (e.g. "Inter-Regular"), so a blind swap breaks every text style.
findings.evidence: app.json plugins array contains bare "expo-font" (no config object) — verified by parsing app.json; src/App.tsx:23-24 imports from @expo-google-fonts/inter + /geist, :77-86 useFonts with 8 weights; measured TTF sizes in root node_modules/@expo-google-fonts (Inter_400Regular.ttf 342,408 B etc.). `grep -rn 'fontFamily: "Inter_400Regular"' src | wc -l` → 277; total fontFamily → 651. Only the 8 imported weights are bundled by Metro (no italics/unused weights) — no waste there.
findings.fix: Option A (recommended, minimal): do nothing — current setup is correct, non-gating, and the swap is one early frame; record this as resolved. Option B (if the owner wants zero font-swap): copy the 8 TTFs into apps/mobile/src/assets/fonts/, configure `["expo-font", {"fonts": ["./src/assets/fonts/Inter_400Regular.ttf", ...]}]` in app.json, prebuild, then verify the iOS-registered names with `UIFont.familyNames` dump — expo-font plugin registers by file, and lookup uses PostScript names ("Inter-Regular", "Geist-Regular" etc.), so add a single mapping shim: replace raw string literals with constants from a new src/ui/fonts.ts (`export const InterRegular = Platform.select(...)`) — a mechanical 651-site codemod (`sed` per weight). Remove useFonts from App.tsx:77-86 and the two @expo-google-fonts deps.
findings.acceptance: Option B only: cold start shows brand fonts on the very first rendered frame (record slow-mo screen capture; no glyph swap); App.tsx has no useFonts; @expo-google-fonts removed from package.json; all screens visually unchanged.
findings.risk: Option B touches 651 style sites — high regression surface for a cosmetic one-frame win; that is why Option A is the recommendation. If done, the PostScript-name mapping must be device-verified per weight (SemiBold/Medium names differ between families).
